description:
Apigee Edge for Public Cloud

Announcement

On November 11, 2026, we began releasing Edge UI updates for Apigee Edge for Public Cloud.

Fixed

Bug ID Component Description
392653797, 399185014 Edge UI Fixed an issue where navigating to the App Details or New App pages in organizations with a large number of API products experienced slowness or UI freezing during the initial page load. The Edge UI now fetches API products on demand when you open the Add Product dialog, improving initial page load performance.
576859695 Edge UI Fixed an issue in the Analytics Error Code Analysis dashboard where 504 Gateway Timeout responses caused by target timeouts were excluded from the Proxy errors charts. Target timeout 504 responses are now counted under Proxy errors.
188163219 Edge UI Fixed a UI formatting issue in the Analytics Custom Reports list view so that dimensions display without overlapping.

Apigee hybrid

Announcement

v1.16.14

On November 11, 2026 we released an updated version of the Apigee hybrid software, v1.16.14.

  • For information about upgrading, see Upgrading Apigee hybrid to v1.16.14.
  • For information about new installations, see The big picture.
Note: This is a patch release. The container images used in patch releases are integrated with the Apigee hybrid Helm charts. Upgrading to a patch by using the Helm chart automatically updates the images. You don't typically need to make manual image changes. For information about container image support in Apigee hybrid releases, see Apigee release process.

Feature

SanitizeUserPrompt and SanitizeModelResponse policies now support function calling

The SanitizeUserPrompt and SanitizeModelResponse policies now handle LLM function calling (tool use) flows. Two new optional XML elements extract function calling content for Model Armor sanitization:

  • <FunctionResponseSource> in SanitizeUserPrompt: extracts function/tool response data from user turns. Used as a fallback when <UserPromptSource> returns empty on function calling turns.
  • <FunctionCallSource> in SanitizeModelResponse: extracts function call arguments from model responses. Used as a fallback when <LLMResponseSource> returns empty.

Default templates target the Gemini format and require no additional configuration. For OpenAI and Anthropic formats, configure custom JSONPath templates. For more information, see FunctionResponseSource and FunctionCallSource.

Fixed

Fixed in this release

Bug ID Description
575563262 Updated the Google Cloud client library stack to match Apigee hybrid 1.17 (protobuf 4.x, gRPC 1.82, GAX 2.83, Guava 33.5). With this update: (1) a malformed inbound gRPC request frame is now reported to the client as grpc-status INTERNAL (13) and recorded in analytics as x-apigee.grpc.status=13, instead of an Apigee ServiceUnavailable fault (UNAVAILABLE, 14) with no x-apigee.grpc.status; (2) an ExternalCallout policy whose Google service account does not exist now fails with gRPC UNAUTHENTICATED (16) instead of UNAVAILABLE (14); and (3) Gson parse-error messages, such as in proxy validation errors, now end with a link to Gson's troubleshooting guide.
572875915 Fixed an issue where the apigee-env Helm chart and Apigee operator ignored the synchronizer pollInterval configuration (synchronizer.pollInterval, envs[].pollInterval, and envs[].components.synchronizer.pollInterval); configured values now take effect, and values below 60 seconds are raised to 60.
572025634 Fixed an issue where responses with a compressed text/event-stream body to a proxy with an EventFlow returned a corrupted body; compressed text/event-stream responses now skip EventFlow processing and pass through intact.
560272924 Apigee hybrid now supports continuous-scan bidirectional gRPC streaming for the SanitizeModelResponse policy over Server-Sent Events (SSE) streams, preserving native LLM provider SSE JSON envelopes and event framing.
555332621 Fixed an issue where Model Armor policies did not honor HTTPClient.managementplane.skip.proxy: when set, Model Armor callouts now bypass the forward proxy like other googleapis traffic, while streaming (ContinuousScan) Model Armor traffic uses the forward proxy.
549779897 Apigee analytics now reports the Model Armor template, verdict, and matched filters for each request on both the prompt and model-response directions.
524115876 Fixed an intermittent HTTP 400 error in the OASValidation policy's strict parameter validation that rejected valid requests under load.
519116013 Disabled weak Diffie-Hellman (DH) TLS cipher suites on port 7070 (Prometheus jmx_exporter) in the apigee-hybrid-cassandra container.
500345401 The apigee-telemetry Helm chart now supports independent tolerations and nodeSelector configuration for the OpenTelemetry Collector (metrics.collector), Prometheus Adapter (metrics.adapter), and Stackdriver Exporters (metrics.proxyStackdriverExporter and metrics.appStackdriverExporter).

BigQuery

Feature

Project caps (also known as scheduling policies) let you limit maximum slots and concurrency per project within a BigQuery reservation. This feature is only supported in the BigQuery Enterprise and Enterprise Plus editions and is generally available (GA).

Feature

You can specify an optional principal property on BigQuery reservation assignments to route queries to specific reservations based on the identity of the user, service account, or third-party identity executing the job. This feature is only supported in the BigQuery Enterprise and Enterprise Plus editions and is generally available (GA).

Feature

You can use the JSON_FLATTEN function to extract all non-array values that are either directly in the input JSON value or children of one or more consecutively nested arrays in the input JSON value. This function is generally available. (GA).

Bug fixes in IntelliJ

Various bug fixes and minor product enhancements.

Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

Feature

End-user safety identifier labels for abuse monitoring

End-user safety_identifier request labels are available in General Availability (GA) for Gemini (generateContent and streamGenerateContent) and Veo (predictLongRunning) API calls. API resellers and multi-tenant apps can pass an anonymized per-user ID in labels to attribute policy violations to individual end users. Targeted attribution helps prevent enforcement actions across an entire Google Cloud project.

For formatting requirements and code samples, see Pass an end-user safety identifier in API calls.

Fixed

CodeMender updates (v0.21.0)

This release introduces updates to CodeMender:

  • Sandboxed build commands and patch refresh: When sandboxing is enabled, cm build and cm fix build validation now run build.command inside the sandbox, and cm fix refreshes stored patch diffs after build validation finishes.
  • Read-only host toolchains and isolated caches: Sandboxed cm build, cm fix, and cm verify runs now mount host toolchain and package-manager directories read-only and redirect supported compiler and package caches to session-scoped temporary directories.
  • Command environment isolation: Disabled repository Git hooks, isolated host Git configuration, and ignored repository Python bytecode caches (__pycache__) during command and build runs.
  • Bug fixes:
    • Added a 30-minute timeout for silent active turns so stalled sessions cancel and recover cleanly.
    • Preserved proof-of-concept execution output when reproducer errors occur, retaining stdout and stderr to help diagnose build failures, timeouts, and setup issues.
    • Fixed an issue where patch generation failed on mid-run sandbox failures by automatically retrying with a fresh sandbox environment.

For more information, see the CodeMender documentation.

Feature

Gemini 4 Carbon in CodeMender (Preview)

CodeMender now supports Gemini 4 Carbon. To use it, pass --model gemini-4-carbon to cm find, cm verify, or cm fix. Gemini 3.8 Flash remains the default model.

For more information, see Specifying the model.

Feature

Govern agents on any CNCF-conformant Kubernetes cluster with Agent Gateway for cross-cloud (Limited Preview)

Agent Gateway for cross-cloud is available in Limited Preview. It extends Agent Platform governance to agents that run on Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF)-conformant Kubernetes clusters outside of Google Cloud, such as Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS), Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), Red Hat OpenShift, and bare-metal clusters. Your agents keep running where they are, but you govern them from one place: give each agent a verifiable identity, register agents and MCP servers in Agent Registry, and route their LLM, MCP, and A2A traffic through local Agent Gateway proxies by using your existing service mesh or network stack. Those proxies enforce access and Model Armor safety policies, and send access logs and agent traces to Cloud Logging and Cloud Trace.

Agent Gateway for cross-cloud is available at no charge during Limited Preview. Other products that you configure with it, such as Model Armor, Cloud Logging, and Cloud Trace, are billed at their standard rates. To request access, complete the access request form.

For more information, see Set up Agent Gateway for cross-cloud.

Google Distributed Cloud (software only) for VMware

Announcement

If you use a third-party storage vendor, check the listing of our previously-qualified storage partners.

Feature

The following changes were added in 1.34.1100-gke.125:

  • Updated system components and container base images to remove the distrusted eMudhra (emSign) and AAA Certificate Services root CAs and reject compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs.
  • Upgraded Container-Optimized OS (COS) to milestone 121 (cos-121-18867-652-7), which removes the distrusted eMudhra (emSign) and AAA Certificate Services root CAs.
  • Updated the Ubuntu 22.04 node and admin workstation base image to ubuntu-gke-op-2204-1-33-v20261024 to remove the distrusted eMudhra (emSign) root CAs (USN-8944-1).

Fixed

The following issues were fixed in 1.34.1100-gke.125:

  • Fixed vulnerabilities listed in Vulnerability fixes.
  • Fixed an issue where deleting a user cluster left an orphaned k8s-health-check-reader-binding-<cluster-namespace> ClusterRoleBinding on the admin cluster. Health check permissions now use a namespaced RoleBinding, and legacy ClusterRoleBinding objects are automatically cleaned up.
  • Fixed an issue where adding IP addresses to an existing MetalLB address pool of an advanced user cluster left the cluster stuck in the UPDATING state. The update is now rejected during validation; to add IP addresses, add a new address pool instead.
  • Fixed an issue where preflight checks erroneously required the control plane VIP (loadBalancer.vips.controlPlaneVIP) to be in the control plane node subnet when the control plane load balancer mode is set to manual.
  • Fixed an issue where audit-proxy retried audit log exports indefinitely on permanent errors, generating excessive audit logging traffic.
  • Fixed an issue where the Kubernetes preflight health check scanned all namespaces in the admin cluster instead of the target cluster's namespace, causing cluster upgrades to fail if an unrelated cluster had stale reconciling resources.

Google Kubernetes Engine

Issue

On nodes that have Linux syscall auditing enabled, such as Container-Optimized OS nodes where you enabled Linux auditd logging, mounting Cloud Storage FUSE CSI driver volumes can hang indefinitely. Pods that use these volumes don't start and remain in a status such as Init:0/1 or ContainerCreating. Pods that are being deleted remain in the Terminating state, and node drains, including drains during node pool upgrades, might not complete. Pod events show errors similar to the following:

MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "VOLUME_NAME" : rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "VOLUME_NAME" : rpc error: code = Aborted desc = An operation with the given volume key TARGET_PATH already exists

The following GKE versions are affected:

  • 1.31.14-gke.2963000 and later
  • 1.32.13-gke.2714000 and later
  • 1.33.13-gke.1973000 and later
  • 1.34.12-gke.1209000 and later
  • 1.35.8-gke.2014000 and later
  • 1.36.5-gke.1817000 and later
  • 1.37.1-gke.1777000 and later

In these versions, the Cloud Storage FUSE CSI driver uses a Debian 13 base image whose mount utility uses the newer Linux mount API. When syscall auditing is active, the mount operation can hang in the kernel before the FUSE file system is initialized. Restarting the gcsfusecsi-node Pod doesn't resolve the issue. Nodes that don't have syscall audit rules loaded aren't affected.

Workaround: Disable Linux auditd logging in clusters that use the Cloud Storage FUSE CSI driver, and then re-create the affected nodes to clear the audit rules that are loaded on them. If you must keep auditd logging enabled, contact Cloud Customer Care.

A fix is in progress.

Feature

Capacity buffers, including active and standby capacity buffers, are generally available for GKE Standard and Autopilot clusters running version 1.37.1-gke.3020000 or later. Capacity buffers let you pre-provision and optionally suspend standby compute capacity using the CapacityBuffer custom resource (autoscaling.x-k8s.io/v1beta1) to accelerate workload scaling and mitigate capacity constraints. To get started, see About capacity buffers.

Announcement

Scheduled maintenance of Management/Control Plane for the Apigee Edge for Public Cloud on November 6, 2026.

Scheduled maintenance of Management/Control Plane for the Apigee Edge for Public Cloud production will take place on Friday, November 6, 2026, from 9:00 PM PT to 10:00 PM PT (Saturday, November 7, 2026, from 5:00 AM UTC to 6:00 AM UTC). This maintenance follows the monthly maintenance window schedule documented in the Apigee Edge release notes archive.

During the scheduled maintenance window, the following services will be temporarily unavailable, and attempts to access them will return a 4xx status code:

  • Management Services UI
  • Management Services APIs
  • Monetization Management APIs
  • New proxy deployments
  • DevPortal Service
  • Microgateway Services
  • Edge Query (Analytics Stats APIs)

Runtime API calls to deployed API proxies are unaffected. While access to analytics queries may be temporarily unavailable during the maintenance window, all analytics and metrics data from this period will be available once maintenance ends.

Apigee hybrid

Announcement

v1.14.10

On November 5, 2026 we released an updated version of the Apigee hybrid software, v1.14.10.

  • For information about upgrading, see Upgrading Apigee hybrid to v1.14.10.
  • For information about new installations, see The big picture.
Note: This is a patch release. The container images used in patch releases are integrated with the Apigee hybrid Helm charts. Upgrading to a patch by using the Helm chart automatically updates the images. You don't typically need to make manual image changes. For information about container image support in Apigee hybrid releases, see Apigee release process.

Fixed

Fixed in this release

Bug ID Description
578314600 Fixed an issue where apigee-connect-agent ignored HTTPS_PROXY and failed to establish a tether in clusters that require an HTTP forward proxy for egress; the agent now uses HTTP/2 keepalive pings on the control-plane connection while honoring HTTPS_PROXY (including proxy credentials).
576707253 Removed the compromised emSign roots and the cross-signing Comodo AAA Services root from the system and Java (cacerts) trust stores across containers.
573622417 Fixed an issue where apigee-ingressgateway forwarded the x-envoy-decorator-operation header to upstream runtime and target backends.
571378258 The apigee-redis container now uses the Valkey engine (version 8.1.10). The RESP2 wire protocol and redis-server and redis-cli binary names are unchanged.
554114419 Fixed an issue where an AssignMessage, HTTPModifier, or RaiseFault policy that creates a new request (createNew="true") in an HTTP/2 flow could not set the :path and :authority pseudo-headers and failed with an invalid-header error.
524115876 Fixed an intermittent HTTP 400 error in the OASValidation policy's strict parameter validation that rejected valid requests under load.
449228485 Fixed an issue where podDisruptionBudget overrides configured in the Helm charts were dropped by the Kubernetes API server.
432315283 Fixed an issue where changes to a multi-certificate truststore's trust anchors required a Message Processor restart when features.truststore.multi_cert_bundle.enabled was toggled at runtime; the outbound SSLContext now rebuilds automatically.

Data Studio

Feature

You can now combine tables vertically in Data Studio blends by using the Union merge operator, which appends rows across up to five tables and removes duplicate rows. In addition, blend UI labels now use merge (such as Merge another table, Merge conditions, and Hide repeated merge fields) to encompass both join and union operations. For more information, see How blends work in Data Studio and Create, edit, and manage blends.

Gemini Enterprise

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Prepaid credits for Pay-as-you-go subscriptions and usage above quota

Prepaid credits are generally available (GA) for self-serve (online) Cloud Billing accounts. You can buy credits to pay for usage without an invoiced billing account. Your billing account's credit balance covers usage in the Pay-as-you-go edition and pay-as-you-go usage above quota in the Gemini Enterprise app, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and AI developer tools, such as Google Antigravity. Pay-as-you-go subscriptions have no license fee because you pay for what you use at pay-as-you-go rates. Cloud Billing still bills your account directly for seat-based license fees in editions such as Standard and Plus.

  • Buy credits and configure auto-reload: Buy prepaid credits, track your balance and transactions, and configure auto-reload with an optional monthly auto-charge limit. Usage is blocked if your credit balance reaches zero or a project reaches its monthly spend limit. Because credits are deducted after usage occurs, your balance might briefly drop below zero if usage occurs before the deduction runs.
  • Use AI developer tools on self-serve accounts: With an upgraded paid self-serve billing account and an active non-trial Gemini Enterprise subscription, you can enable AI developer tools and pay with prepaid credits for Pay-as-you-go edition usage or pay-as-you-go usage above quota. Eligible editions include Standard, Plus, eligible Standard Emerging Market, and Pay-as-you-go. Free-trial subscriptions, free-tier billing accounts, and reseller-managed subaccounts aren't eligible.
  • Monitor costs and invoices: View 30-day costs across the Gemini Enterprise app, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and AI developer tools, and view and download prepayment and monthly consumption invoices.

For more information, see:

  • Manage prepaid credits
  • Configure pay-as-you-go usage above quota
  • Quotas and pricing for the Pay-as-you-go edition
  • AI developer tools overview
  • View costs

Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

Feature

Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash

Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash (gemini-omni-1.2-flash) is available in General Availability (GA). Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is an omni-modal foundation model that processes text, image, and video inputs to generate text and high-definition video with synchronized audio through the Interactions API.

Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash introduces the following capabilities:

  • Standalone video upscaling: Upscale previously generated videos from 360p to 720p or 1080p, and from 720p to 1080p or 4K using task: "upscale". See Upscale videos.

  • Extended video generation and editing duration: Generate or edit videos up to 15 seconds in length across text-to-video, image-to-video, reference-to-video, and video editing tasks (up to 10 seconds for first-and-last-frame interpolation and video extension).

  • Reference-guided video editing and extension: Supply up to 2 reference images along with an input video when editing or extending videos. See Edit videos and Extend videos.

  • Deterministic generation and billing labels: Specify seed for reproducible video outputs and attach custom labels to Interactions API requests.

  • Standard PayGo and Provisioned Throughput: Available with Standard Pay-as-you-go (PayGo) and Provisioned Throughput (685 tokens per second per GSU).

Feature

Interactions API long decodes for Gemini 4 Argon

Long decodes up to 1,048,576 tokens (minus input tokens) on the Interactions API (v1beta1) are available in General Availability (GA) for Gemini 4 Argon (gemini-4-argon and gemini-4-argon-cyber-permissive). You can extend single-turn outputs beyond the per-segment limit (65,536 streaming or 32,768 non-streaming tokens) using automatic continuation in the Google Gen AI SDK (google-genai >= 2.34.0 for Python, @google/genai >= 2.32.0 for JavaScript/TypeScript, Go >= 1.77.0, and Java >= 1.80.0), server-managed background execution (background=true), or custom stored (store=true) and stateless (store=false) continuation_token loops.

For code samples, continuation options, and implementation rules, see Long decodes in the developer's guide to Gemini 4 Argon.

Negative backend deadlines are no longer deprecated

The deprecation of negative backend deadline values announced on October 23, 2026 is withdrawn. In an OpenAPI 2.0 x-google-backend extension or a gRPC BackendRule, a negative deadline continues to use the default deadline, the same as 0, and won't be rejected. OpenAPI 3.x backends still reject a negative deadline.

Syncing data from BigQuery into AlloyDB is generally available (GA). This feature lets you copy or mirror analytical tables from BigQuery into AlloyDB for low-latency operational access using the alloydb_sync extension.

AlloyDB Express is available in Preview for PostgreSQL 18. Optimized for rapid prototyping and for workflows that use AI coding agents, this configuration provides the following features:

To upgrade, install version 3.3.12 of the edgemicro npm package or pull the gcr.io/apigee-microgateway/edgemicro:3.3.12 Docker image. For the npm upgrade steps, see Upgrading Edge Microgateway. For earlier Edge Microgateway releases, see Edge Microgateway release notes.

Breaking

Removed support for Node.js 20 from Edge Microgateway. Use Node.js 22, 24, or 26 instead.

Edge Microgateway 3.3.12 supports only Node.js 22, 24, and 26. Support for Node.js 26 is new in this release. Before you upgrade an npm installation of Edge Microgateway to 3.3.12, upgrade the Node.js runtime on each host to version 22, 24, or 26. The 3.3.12 Docker image is built on Node.js 24, so Docker deployments need no action for this change. For supported versions, see Supported software and supported versions.

Breaking

Removed the npm and npx command-line tools from the Edge Microgateway Docker image. Install custom plugin dependencies before you add the plugins to the container.

Starting with version 3.3.12, the Edge Microgateway Docker image doesn't include npm or npx, and commands that run either tool inside the container fail. The change doesn't affect how Edge Microgateway runs. If your custom plugins have npm dependencies, run npm install in each plugin directory before you add the plugins to the container, so that each plugin's node_modules directory is included. For the steps, see Adding a custom plugin. This change doesn't affect npm installations of Edge Microgateway.

The following changes were added in 1.35.700-gke.124:

  • Updated system components and container base images to remove the distrusted eMudhra (emSign) and AAA Certificate Services root CAs and reject compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs.

Fixed

The following issues were fixed in 1.35.700-gke.124:

  • Fixed vulnerabilities listed in Vulnerability fixes.
  • Fixed an issue where removing a node from a cluster left behind its local PersistentVolume resources instead of garbage collecting them. This fix applies to Google Distributed Cloud for bare metal local PersistentVolume resources created after upgrading to 1.35.700-gke.124; existing orphaned PersistentVolume resources must be deleted manually.
  • Fixed an issue where resetting or removing a control plane node could remove the wrong etcd or etcd-events member if another control plane node's IP address shared the same prefix (for example, 10.201.0.2 and 10.201.0.26), causing the affected node to become NotReady and stalling cluster upgrades.
  • Improved containerd resilience against state corruption if a node reboots while unpacking container images.
  • Fixed an issue where the periodic configuration drift health check failed with a version not supported error while a cluster upgrade or rollback was in progress.
  • Fixed an issue where audit-proxy retried audit log exports indefinitely on permanent errors, generating excessive audit logging traffic.
  • Fixed an issue where the Kubernetes preflight health check scanned all namespaces in the admin cluster instead of the target cluster's namespace, causing cluster upgrades to fail if an unrelated cluster had stale reconciling resources.

The Consolidated Settings and Navigation feature is now in public preview. It replaces the separate SIEM Settings and SOAR Settings menus with a single Settings menu, grouped into Administration, Access Management, Investigation, Detection and Data Management, and also updates the left navigation menu. Lakehouse caching for cross-cloud data access is generally available (GA). Cross-cloud caching is disabled by default. You can opt in to caching on a Lakehouse federated catalog or a BigQuery cross-cloud connection to cache remote files in your Google Cloud region. This helps reduce cross-cloud egress costs and accelerate subsequent queries.

For more information, see About cross-cloud data access and Query remote data.

Feature

Lakehouse supports the following remote catalog providers for cross-cloud data access. This feature is generally available (GA).

  • Databricks Unity Catalog on Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud
  • AWS Glue Data Catalog on AWS
  • Snowflake Horizon Catalog on AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud
  • Workday Data Lake on AWS or Google Cloud

This feature lets you configure federated catalog endpoints to synchronize catalog metadata and query Apache Iceberg tables in remote catalogs directly from Google Cloud using BigQuery, Managed Service for Apache Spark, and Apache Spark without migrating data or building complex ETL pipelines. You can route background metadata refresh and queries over the public internet or privately over Cross-Cloud Interconnect, and protect cross-cloud data access with VPC Service Controls service perimeters. For Databricks Unity Catalog, you can also use user identity federation to propagate end-user identities on queries for permission enforcement and audit logging.

For more information, see About cross-cloud data access, Query remote data, and Use VPC Service Controls with federated catalog endpoints.

Feature

You can now monitor the performance, adoption, latency, and costs of your data agents and their conversations by using Google Cloud Observability in BigQuery. This feature is generally available (GA).

Feature

You can use the AI.PARSE_DOCUMENT function to extract layout elements such as titles, headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, and images by using the Document AI layout parser to convert unstructured documents into structured JSON data.

This function is generally available (GA).

Feature

You can now use BigQuery change history and continuous queries for Apache Iceberg managed tables in Lakehouse.

You can use the APPENDS table-valued function (TVF) to track rows appended to Apache Iceberg managed tables over a specified time range, and use BigQuery continuous queries to read incoming data from and write output rows to Apache Iceberg managed tables.

This feature is generally available (GA).

For more information, see Work with change history and Introduction to continuous queries.

Feature

The SECURE_CONTEXT function is now available in Preview. SECURE_CONTEXT returns the value of a request-scoped secure context parameter provided at query runtime, allowing logical views to dynamically filter and evaluate data based on context variables such as user attributes, department IDs, or tenant identifiers.

Feature

The Data Engineering Agent now supports BigQuery AI, ML, and object functions and statements in generated Dataform SQLX pipelines and agent instruction files.

This feature is generally available (GA).

Distributed tracing with Cloud Trace is available in Preview for Global external Application Load Balancers, Regional external Application Load Balancers, Regional internal Application Load Balancers, and Cross-region internal Application Load Balancers. For more information, see Distributed tracing overview.

Feature

For mutual TLS (mTLS) on Application Load Balancers, frontend mTLS validation relaxations are generally available.

The ALLOW_VALIDATION_RELAXATIONS client validation mode on the Client Authentication (ServerTlsPolicy) resource allows you to configure specific X.509 certificate validation exceptions to standard client certificate validation rules. This simplifies migrations of legacy workloads while maintaining an active security posture.

This mode supports the following client certificate validation relaxation parameters:

  • ALLOW_MISSING_EKU: Bypasses Extended Key Usage validation if the EKU extension is absent in the client certificate.

  • ALLOW_SHA1_HASHING: Permits client certificates signed with the legacy SHA-1 algorithm.

  • ALLOW_EXPIRED_LEAF_CERTIFICATE: Evaluates expired leaf certificates by validating them as of 1 second prior to their actual expiration time.

This feature is available for all Application Load Balancer types.

For more information, see Client validation modes.

Advanced malware sandbox (WildFire) integrates dynamic machine learning (ML) and cloud-based behavioral sandboxing to perform deep inspection of network-routed file transfers and block zero-day malware before it reaches your workloads. Feature

Breaking

Permissions to grant access by using Unified Access Policies (UAPs) are included in the following roles:

  • Owner (roles/owner)
  • Admin (roles/admin)
  • Security Admin (roles/iam.securityAdmin)
  • Organization Administrator (roles/resourcemanager.organizationAdmin)
  • Folder IAM Admin (roles/resourcemanager.folderIamAdmin)
  • Project IAM Admin (roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin)

If users have these roles and aren't denied permission to modify UAPs or bind them to resources, then they can grant any permission by using UAPs. Granting access in this way is not limited by custom organization policies that limit role granting.

If you want to prevent these users from granting access by using UAPs, do one of the following:

  • Enforce the iam.managed.disableAccessPolicyBinding organization policy constraint in your organization.
  • Deny UAP-related access change permissions to principals with these roles.

Announcement

Starting November 1, 2026, at 02:00 a.m. local time, unpatched Cloud SQL for MySQL instances that evaluate certain local Canadian time zones (across Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, and Northwest Territories) will lag by one hour because the instances still follow the autumn fall back schedule. Stored timestamp data isn't modified.

What should I do?

Before November 1, 2026, do one of the following fixes:

  • Apply self-service maintenance (Recommended): If your applications rely on database functions to calculate, schedule, or display times in these Canadian time zones (such as Calgary, Edmonton, Vancouver, or Winnipeg), then update your instances to the latest maintenance release using the Google Cloud console or the gcloud CLI.

    Updated time zone rules that reflect permanent standard daylight offsets across Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, and Northwest Territories are supported in Cloud SQL for MySQL maintenance release *.R20260726.00_36 or later.

    For more information, see Perform self-service maintenance.

  • Database configuration stopgap: If your organization can't restart instances before November 1, 2026, then you can set the time zone for your database session without causing downtime for your instance. Set the default_time_zone flag for the database session to your target fixed numeric offset (for example, '-06:00' for Alberta, '-07:00' for British Columbia, or '-05:00' for Manitoba).

    For more information about configuring database flags, see Configure database flags.

Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL

Announcement

Starting November 1, 2026, at 02:00 a.m. local time, unpatched Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instances that evaluate certain local Canadian time zones (across Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, and Northwest Territories) will lag by one hour because the instances still follow the autumn fall back schedule. Stored timestamp data isn't modified.

What should I do?

Before November 1, 2026, do one of the following fixes:

  • Apply self-service maintenance (Recommended): If your applications rely on database functions to calculate, schedule, or display times in these Canadian time zones (such as Calgary, Edmonton, Vancouver, or Winnipeg), then update your instances to the latest maintenance release using the Google Cloud console or the gcloud CLI.

    Updated time zone rules that reflect permanent standard daylight offsets across Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, and Northwest Territories are supported in Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL maintenance release *.R20260712.01_44 or later.

    For more information, see Perform self-service maintenance.

  • Database configuration stopgap: If your organization can't restart instances before November 1, 2026, then you can set your database session time zone without downtime to an anchor zone.

    ALTER DATABASE database_name SET timezone TO 'anchor_zone';

    Replace the following:

    • database_name: the name of your database.

    • anchor_zone: the anchor zone to use as the time zone for your database. Specify an anchor zone that operates on a permanent offset.

      For example, 'America/Regina' for Alberta and Northwest Territories (UTC-6), 'America/Whitehorse' for British Columbia (UTC-7), or 'America/Coral_Harbour' for Manitoba (UTC-5).

Cloud SQL for SQL Server

Announcement

Starting November 1, 2026, at 02:00 a.m. local time, Cloud SQL for SQL Server instances that evaluate certain local Canadian time zones (across Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, and Northwest Territories) will lag by one hour because the instances still follow the autumn fall back schedule. Stored timestamp data isn't modified.

What should I do?

For SQL Server, Microsoft has published guidance, recommending updating each applicable instance's time zone to the Windows time zone with the matching fixed offset.

Update each instance's time zone to the Windows time zone with the matching fixed offset:

Jurisdiction Current time zone Recommended time zone Fixed offset
British Columbia Pacific Standard Time Yukon Standard Time UTC-07:00
Alberta / Inuvik, NWT Mountain Standard Time Canada Central Standard Time UTC-06:00
Manitoba Central Standard Time Eastern Standard Time (Mexico) UTC-05:00

You can make the change in the Google Cloud console (Edit instance > Flags and parameters > Time zone) or with gcloud:

gcloud sql instances patch INSTANCE_NAME \
  --project=PROJECT_ID \
  --time-zone="Yukon Standard Time"

Gemini Enterprise

Feature

Gemini Notebook Enterprise: Visual refresh

This update includes the following changes and features. These features are generally available (GA):

  • Refreshed UI design: The user interface features an updated color scheme and style that match the consumer and Google Workspace versions of Gemini Notebook.

  • Audio overview language selection: You can choose the language for the audio overview output. This lets you create an audio output in a language different from the notebook's language (Settings > Output language).

  • Infographic update: You can see examples of the visual style before you choose one for your infographic.

  • Customize the notebook summary: You can replace the autogenerated summary of the notebook with your own custom summary. Select Customize notebook from the more_vert More options menu.

  • Sharing notebooks: When you notify people that you're sharing a notebook with them, you no longer have the option to write a welcome note.

  • Fast Research on the web: Web and Fast Research replace Discover sources. The I'm feeling curious button is no longer available.

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: S&P Global - Adaptive Retrieval data store (Preview)

The S&P Global - Adaptive Retrieval data store is available in Public Preview in Gemini Enterprise. You can use natural language to ask questions about the S&P Global data your S&P Global account is entitled to access. For more information, see Connect a third-party data source.

Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

Feature

Inference request metadata logging (GA)

Inference request metadata logging is generally available. Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform can write one Cloud Logging entry for every inference request your project serves. Each entry records the model, region, consumption option, token counts, Provisioned Throughput usage, latency and error code. Entries record metadata only and never contain prompts or responses. Logging is supported for Gemini models that use generateContent and streamGenerateContent, and for Claude models that use rawPredict and streamRawPredict.

You can turn on logging in the Google Cloud console, from the Provisioned Throughput page, or with the REST API. Turning on logging in the console also turns on detailed metrics, which chart Provisioned Throughput traffic at one-second resolution. With logging on, the model observability dashboard adds 1-second resolution options to its charts for pay-as-you-go traffic. To attribute usage to a team, application or tenant, add request headers with the x-goog-agent-platform-observability-label- prefix, and query the entries with SQL in Observability Analytics.

For more information, see Log inference request metadata.

Feature

Computer use tool is available in General Availability

The Computer use tool is available in General Availability (GA). This release introduces comprehensive Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) safety governance, enabling developers to selectively configure or override specific confirmation policies (such as financial transactions or data modification) while allowing administrators to mandate organization-wide guardrails using the configurableComputerUseToolSafetyPolicies constraint.

Looker

Announcement

On November 1, 2026, several Canadian provinces and territories—Manitoba, Alberta, British Columbia, and parts of the Northwest Territories—transition to permanent daylight saving time (DST) or remain on their summer UTC offsets year-round. On unpatched Looker instances, these changes affect scheduled content delivery fire times and table calculations that use now() with the affected Canadian time zones (America/Winnipeg, Canada/Central, America/Rainy_River, America/Edmonton, Canada/Mountain, America/Vancouver, Canada/Pacific, and America/Inuvik). Patched Looker builds update the scheduler (Ruby) and browser (JavaScript) time zone data, while server-evaluated now() table calculations on the JVM still use the bundled JDK time zone database (tzdb 2026b). To learn how to upgrade to a patched Looker build or configure an alternative schedule delivery time zone, see 2026 Canadian time zone changes.

Managed Service for Apache Airflow

Issue

Starting October 24, 2026, Managed Airflow (Gen 3) and Managed Airflow (Gen 2) environments running Python 3.11 with google-api-core package versions 2.28.0 to 2.43.0 (including versions 2.30.3 to 2.43.0, which weren't previously affected) might experience degraded performance because of a Python 3.11 deprecation check that scans installed package metadata on every new Python subprocess import. You might observe increased DAG parsing times, longer task execution times, higher CPU usage on Airflow DAG processors and workers, and frequent FutureWarning log entries from google/api_core/_python_version_support.py about Python 3.11 support ending on 2027-10-24.

For the list of affected builds and available workarounds (installing google-api-core>=2.43.1 on compatible Airflow 3 builds or applying a sitecustomize.py runtime patch), see the known issue for Managed Airflow (Gen 3) or Managed Airflow (Gen 2).

NetApp Volumes

Announcement

Google Cloud NetApp Volumes now supports the Flex Unified service level, including custom performance, in the following regions:

  • northamerica-northeast1 (Montréal)

  • northamerica-northeast2 (Toronto)

For more information about available regions, see Supported regions.

Resource Manager

Feature

Preview: Management boundaries and capability configurations in Resource Manager are available in Preview. Management boundaries establish dynamic, tag-based or hierarchy-wide administrative perimeters across multiple Google Cloud projects. This feature lets you centralize resource discovery and governance from a designated management project. You can configure BoundaryConfig, Boundary, and CapabilityConfig resources using Google Cloud CLI to partition projects by Tags values and enable management capabilities for Agent Registry.

For more information, see Management boundaries overview and Configure management boundaries.

SAP on Google Cloud

Announcement

Google SecOps for SAP is generally available (GA)

Google SecOps for SAP is generally available (GA). This solution helps you protect your enterprise SAP applications by integrating business-critical telemetry into Google SecOps to provide unified visibility, threat detection, and security response capabilities.

This release includes:

  • Log ingestion from SAP RISE and self-managed SAP environments that run on Google Cloud, on-premises, or other clouds.
  • SAP-specific YARA-L threat detection rules available in the Google SecOps Detection Rules GitHub repository.
  • Automated threat response and containment capabilities by using the SAP RFC Gateway and SOAR playbooks (Preview).

For more information, see Secure SAP applications with Google SecOps.

Secure Source Manager

Feature

You can now enable vulnerability scanning to detect known vulnerabilities in your dependencies.

Spanner

Feature

Spanner supports equality and ordering comparisons on JSONB and JSON values. You can use these values in GROUP_BY and ORDER BY clauses without first converting them to another data type.

In GoogleSQL, you can also convert other data types to JSON using CAST(expression AS JSON) and compare JSON values directly with non-JSON values. Spanner can implicitly coerces the non-JSON value to JSON for comparison.

Additionally, you can use search indexes to accelerate equality comparisons such as = or IN on JSONB and JSON columns and subpaths.

For more information, see JSON comparison and sorting , JSON comparison coercion , CAST AS JSON , JSON search indexes , and Working with JSONB.

Feature

Spanner Graph supports the following enhancements:

  • You can create property graphs from SQL views that call remote functions (Preview) to compute node and edge properties. For more information, see Compute properties with remote functions.
  • You can write simplified queries on schemaless dynamic properties without explicit conversions to SQL data types. This lets you group and sort dynamic properties, and compare them directly with literal values or other dynamic properties. For more information, see Filter, compare, and sort by dynamic properties and JSON comparison and sorting.

reCAPTCHA

Change

Fraud Defense Mobile SDK v18.9.4 is available for Android. This version includes the following:

  • Fixes a memory leak where destroyed activities were retained by lifecycle callbacks (Issue #194).
  • Fixes a dependency compatibility issue with Kotlin Coroutines and POM API dependencies.

title: October 23, 2026
description:
API Gateway

Deprecated

Negative backend deadlines are deprecated

A negative backend deadline in an OpenAPI 2.0 x-google-backend extension or a gRPC BackendRule uses the default deadline, the same as 0. Negative values there are deprecated and will be rejected in a future release; until then, creating an API config with one returns a warning in the operation metadata. OpenAPI 3.x backends already reject a negative deadline. To use the default, omit the field or set it to 0.

For more information, see OpenAPI 2.0 extensions and OpenAPI 3.x extensions.

Cloud Database Migration Service

Security

On Saturday, October 17, 2026, Google received a report from a security researcher regarding the compromise of private keys associated with eight eMudhra subordinate Certification Authority (CA) certificates, including those cross-signed by AAA Certificate Services. Consequently, these CA certificates are no longer trusted and are being revoked.

To continue connecting to a source database after its CA certificate is updated, upload the new CA certificate to the Database Migration Service source connection profile:

  • Update the connection profile using gcloud database-migration connection-profiles update or the connectionProfiles.patch API method.
  • Modify the connection profile in the Google Cloud console:
    • MySQL connection profiles
    • PostgreSQL to Cloud SQL connection profiles
    • PostgreSQL to AlloyDB for PostgreSQL connection profiles
    • Oracle to Cloud SQL connection profiles
    • Oracle to AlloyDB for PostgreSQL connection profiles
    • SQL Server to Cloud SQL connection profiles
    • SQL Server to AlloyDB for PostgreSQL connection profiles

For more information, see security bulletin GCP-2026-071.

Cloud Monitoring

Fixed

Ops Agent version 2.73.0 includes patches for a Go vulnerability involving system root certificates, CVE-2026-111943. For more information, see Ops Agent 2.73.0 notes.

Cloud SQL for MySQL

Security

In response to GCP-2026-071, Google is updating Cloud SQL's managed components. No manual updates to the certificate store are required for Cloud SQL-managed instances. The fix is shipping in a new maintenance version that will be applied during scheduled maintenance. You can also apply the fix by performing self-service maintenance. An announcement will be published when the self-service maintenance fix is available.

What should I do?

  • If you use the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy, then upgrade the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy to 2.26.3 or later and the Cloud SQL Proxy Operator to 1.8.4 or later. If you run the standalone proxy binary, then also update the host's certificate authority (CA) certificates.

  • If you use a Cloud SQL Language Connector, then update the language runtime and operating system CA certificates used with the Cloud SQL Language Connector (for example, Go 1.26.10 or 1.27.3 or later, certifi 2026.10.19 or later).

  • If you're using the gcloud CLI to install the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy, then update the gcloud CLI to 590.0.1.

title: October 21, 2026
description:
Apigee X

Announcement

Apigee Emulator

Apigee Emulator v2.0.2

On October 21, 2026, we released Apigee Emulator version 2.0.2.

This release upgrades the Apigee Emulator runtime to Java 21 (Eclipse Temurin JRE 21) to align local proxy development and policy execution with the production Apigee runtime, while keeping the embedded Apache Cassandra datastore pinned to Java 8. It also addresses 46 security vulnerabilities across Netty, Jackson, Apache Log4j, BouncyCastle, Apache CXF, Eclipse Jetty, and the embedded Cassandra Go standard library health-check binary.

The emulator image is available at Artifact Registry.

To upgrade, update the emulator version in your Cloud Code for VS Code settings to 2.0.2. See Manage the Apigee Emulator for details.

Feature

Apigee Emulator

Changed in this release

  • Upgraded the Apigee Emulator runtime JVM to Eclipse Temurin JRE 21 (21.0.12.1.0+1-0, from JRE 11 11.0.31+11), adding JVM 21 compatibility flags (-Djava.security.manager=allow and --add-opens module flags) for JavaCallout, JavaScript (Rhino), and Python (Jython) policies while keeping the embedded Apache Cassandra 4.0.19 datastore pinned to Eclipse Temurin JRE 8.
  • Upgraded Netty to 4.1.137.Final (from 4.1.135.Final) and updated netty-tcnative-boringssl-static and netty-tcnative-classes to 2.0.81.Final (from 2.0.77.Final).
  • Upgraded Jackson (jackson-core, jackson-databind, and jackson-dataformat-yaml) to 2.21.7 (from 2.18.6 and 2.19.2) and jackson-annotations to 2.21.
  • Upgraded shaded Apache Log4j (log4j-api and log4j-core) in ConfigUtil.jar to 2.25.5 (from 2.17.1 and 2.25.4).
  • Upgraded BouncyCastle (bcprov-jdk18on, bcpkix-jdk18on, and bcutil-jdk18on) to 1.85 (from 1.84).
  • Upgraded Apache CXF (cxf-*) to 3.6.12 (from 3.5.11).
  • Upgraded gRPC to 1.82.3 (from 1.62.2), Protobuf (protobuf-java and protobuf-java-util) to 4.33.6 (from 3.25.5), and Guava to 33.5.0-jre (from 33.4.8-jre).
  • Removed unused org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-* (9.4.58.v20250814) and commons-collections:commons-collections (3.2.2) JARs from the emulator distribution.
  • Refreshed the Cassandra base image to pick up Go standard library 1.27.0 (from 1.25.11) in the embedded /opt/apigee/ready health-check binary.

v1.15.9

Fixed

CodeMender updates (v0.16.0)

This release introduces updates to CodeMender:

  • Deep scan by default (cm find): cm find now runs a concurrent file-by-file deep scan (--deep) by default for higher vulnerability recall across repositories. To run a single-session quick scan instead, pass the --quick flag (cm find --quick). cm stats now breaks down scan usage by mode (--deep, --quick, and --diff).
  • Pre-flight health checks (cm health): Added the cm health command (with --json, --strict, and --timeout flags) to verify credentials, configuration, endpoint reachability, and project authorization before running scans.
  • Expanded file discovery: cm find now scans .hh, .hxx, .inl, and .ipp C++ headers, extensionless scripts with supported language shebangs (python, node, ruby, and php), nested build/, target/, obj/, and bin/ source directories, and production code under spec/, locale/, and i18n/.
  • Bug fixes:
    • Restricted cm verify file writes to .exploit/ inside the project root and skipped missing or out-of-scope session artifacts during workspace restore.
    • Capped single-turn file reads at 256 KiB with pagination hints, bounded unified diff generation on large files, and raised run_command default and maximum timeouts to 120 seconds and 300 seconds.
    • Fixed an issue where sandboxed sessions could not write tool call entries to ~/.codemender/audit.log.
    • Updated multi-file --deep and --diff scans to report INCOMPLETE status when one or more file scans fail.

For more information, see the CodeMender documentation.

description:

Fixed

Fixed dataset and table search in the BigQuery panel, which sometimes failed to return results. Root cause is due to Datacatalog API being sunsetted in favor of Dataplex API.

Apigee X

Announcement

On October 20th, 2026, we began maintenance updates of Apigee instances configured for maintenance windows.

If you set a preferred window for maintenance for your instance, and your instance version is below 1-18-0-apigee-6, your instance will be updated to 1-18-0-apigee-6 within the next seven to 21 days. A notification containing the expected date of upgrade will be sent within the next two business days.

Note: Instances that meet either of the following two criteria will not be updated:
  • Your instance has a DNS misconfiguration, as described in Known Issue 445936920.
  • Your instance uses an Apigee Java Library that has been removed, as described in Apigee release notes dated October 16, 2025.

For more information on participating in scheduled maintenance windows, see Maintenance overview and Manage Apigee instance maintenance windows.

Cloud Workstations

Feature

Cloud Workstations supports automatic failover for boost configurations in Preview. When you enable automatic failover, Cloud Workstations automatically provisions a workstation VM using the boost configuration if Compute Engine lacks capacity for the default machine type during startup.

Gemini Enterprise

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Antigravity Enterprise Gateway support

Antigravity Enterprise Gateway lets organizations route model inference requests from the Antigravity app, Antigravity CLI, and Antigravity for IDEs through a centralized enterprise gateway before forwarding them to Google Cloud. This deployment enables organizations to inspect and audit model traffic, enforce custom security and network egress policies, and authenticate developers through a gateway API key without requiring individual Google Account sign-in.

Requests routed through Antigravity Enterprise Gateway use a centralized Google Cloud service account and are billed on a pay-as-you-go (PAYG) consumption basis through the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. This deployment model doesn't use your Gemini Enterprise seat-based subscription quotas (such as included Standard or Plus monthly allowances). You can't use a gateway and sign in with a Google Account at the same time. If you want to use your included subscription quota instead, disable the enterprise gateway and sign in with your Google Account.

This feature is generally available (GA).

For more information, see:

  • Deploy Antigravity Enterprise Gateway
  • Connect Antigravity to an Enterprise Gateway.

Breaking

Gemini Enterprise: Gemini 2.5 Pro discontinued in Canada and Japan

Gemini 2.5 Pro has been discontinued for in-country Gemini Enterprise app deployments in Canada and Japan. Agents and chat sessions in these regions that previously used Gemini 2.5 Pro automatically switch to in-country Gemini 3.5 Flash.

Gemini 2.5 Pro remains available in the global, us, and eu regions.

For more information, see Data residency for Gemini Enterprise and Manage web app features.

Fixed

A security issue in GKE fleet management that could have allowed unauthorized configuration changes to clusters registered to a fleet has been resolved. The fixes are rolled out to all regions, and no action is required.

This issue has been resolved. You can upgrade your cluster control plane to the following versions to fix the issue for ubuntu_containerd and older cos_containerd node pools:

  • Specific 1.36.4 mitigation patches: 1.36.4-gke.1247001, 1.36.4-gke.1247002, 1.36.4-gke.1391001, 1.36.4-gke.1391003, 1.36.4-gke.1495001, 1.36.4-gke.1495003, 1.36.4-gke.2046001, 1.36.4-gke.2202002

Feature

Spanner supports approximate aggregate functions for both GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL dialects. These functions produce statistical estimates of distinct counts, allowing you to compute results faster and save resources on large datasets compared to exact aggregation.

For more information, see approximate aggregate functions (GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL), HyperLogLog++ functions, and Sketches.

title: AI’s role in the creative process
description: Which parts of the creative process can AI do for us—and which do we insist on keeping for ourselves?

title: Workflow lab: Test ideas with code layers and the Figma agent

title: Design system 104: Making metrics matter
description: Behind every successful design system lies a surprising secret: numbers. Learn how tracking the right metrics can transform your design system from a helpful resource into a powerful engine for efficiency.

title: Double click: Human takes on agentic AI
description: There’s a lot of buzz about AI agents. Robots that do more with less supervision—what could go wrong? We asked our community how this might shake up how we think about UX.

description: As part of our first-ever Sustainability Week, we’re sharing an update on our climate investments—and some of the ways Figma helps other companies build green initiatives of their own.

title: Issue no.9: Memos for the future
description: In a time of blurred roles, new technology, and breakneck product cycles, how do we uphold craft and purpose in our work?

title: A2UI 1.0: Build delightful, fast, reliable, agentic experiences
description: A2UI 1.0 is an open protocol for generative UI that enables AI agents to render interactive, native screens across web, mobile, and desktop applications. Developers can leverage open-source renderer SDKs—including React, Angular, Lit, Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose—alongside agent SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and Dart. The release introduces bidirectional function calls, swappable inference formats, and secure data binding to help teams seamlessly integrate generative UI into their product stacks.

title: DevFest is back!
description: DevFest 2026 runs from October 1 to December 31, bringing together nearly a million developers across more than 800 global events centered on the agentic AI era. Under the theme "Build, Secure, Scale," participants gain hands-on experience with Google’s developer stack—including Gemini, Google AI Studio, Google Antigravity, and Web MCP—through live workshops and codelabs. The conference focuses on enabling developers to prototype rapidly, ensure secure and private deployments, and leverage production-ready infrastructure.

title: Building Conversational Commerce with Multi-Agent Swarms on GCP: A Working Prototype
description: This document provides a publication template and metadata structure for a technical blog post focused on building Conversational User Interfaces (CUIs) using AI. It outlines key developer focus areas, product stacks, and approval workflows required for publishing technical content through Google Developer Studio. The framework helps engineers organize their guides and solutions to effectively share AI-driven conversational interface designs with the developer community.

title: Fast, reliable A2UI, with swappable inference formats
description: A2UI now supports swappable inference formats, introducing A2UI Express which uses up to 3x fewer tokens and cuts latency by compiling compact Python-style syntax into standard A2UI JSON via Agent SDKs. Developers can also use controlled generation with TypeSafe's Jev system-decision models to render known-shape screens in under 300 ms while smaller models stream text. These updates require no changes to frontend renderers or component catalogs, offering flexible performance levers for generative UI development across Python, TypeScript, and Dart.

title: Daemons can now send traces to Vercel Tracing
description:
Vercel Daemons can now send OpenTelemetry traces to Vercel Tracing, allowing you and your agents to inspect background worker operations alongside the rest of your project's traces.

Vercel provides each daemon with a Unix socket for receiving OTLP/HTTP traces and sets the socket's path in VERCEL_OTEL_SOCKET_PATH.

Upgrading @vercel/otel to version 2.3.0 or later enables automatic trace export for Node.js daemons using the default configuration. The SDK detects this socket and sends the spans your worker records to Vercel.

These spans are available through the Vercel CLI, which can search by service name within a project and return JSON for your agents.

Learn more in the daemon tracing documentation.

Read more

description:
Vercel Token Pass now includes $150 of tokens per month (up from $80) for the same $30 per team per month.

The credit applies to featured open-weight models served through AI Gateway, including Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1 Pro, GLM 5.3, GLM 5.3 Flash, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.

Credit resets each billing period with no rollover. When it runs out, requests using standard AI Gateway keys or OIDC tokens fall back to the team's AI Gateway balance, while requests using Token Pass-scoped keys stop with no overage charges.

Token Pass is an Early Access add-on for Pro teams, with limited spots and a waitlist when they fill. To connect your coding agent, run vercel token-pass in the Vercel CLI, or use a Token Pass API key if your agent supports AI Gateway.

Subscribe to Token Pass in your AI Gateway dashboard.

description:

Pass credentials: { npm: true } when creating a sandbox to let it use your team's existing npm credentials.

Tokens stay outside the sandbox. The firewall adds authentication to install requests sent to your configured registries, so a coding agent can install dependencies without seeing the tokens.

Update your Sandbox SDK or CLI to the latest version.

Read the npm credentials documentation to get started.

description:
Gemini Decision 1 from Google is now available on AI Gateway. The multimodal decision model works with text, images, audio, video, and PDF documents, returning Boolean probabilities, choices, and scores. Use it to route requests, check policies, filter agent tools, or rank results without generating output tokens.

title: Introducing Vercel Schedules
description:
Cron jobs are useful for work that needs to happen regularly. You can use them to do things such as back up your database on a schedule, or keep data in sync between two systems.

You define them once in code and then can update them by editing their config and redeploying. But today, agents interact with users as work evolves, and schedules need to be updated in real time.

We built Vercel Schedules to allow agents and applications to create, change, or cancel one-time and recurring schedules through code, without redeploying.

What are Vercel Schedules?

Schedules builds on the static approach used by Vercel Cron Jobs, but are designed to let users and agents decide when work should happen while your application is still running. A schedule tells Vercel when to trigger a task and where to send it. Your application provides the code that carries out the work.

You can use schedules for both static and dynamic jobs:

  • Static schedules keep the timing in vercel.json or Build Output API configuration and sync when you deploy. You can use them to call private functions or HTTP paths, or send messages to Queue topics.

  • Dynamic schedules let your app create and manage schedules through the JS SDK, CLI, or API as it runs. They support one-time and recurring work through Queue topics.

You can also test scheduled work on Preview deployments and in custom environments before running it in Production.

How Schedules works

Take this example: A user could ask an agent with web access, “Tomorrow morning, summarize the top five stories on Hacker News.” The traditional solution would be storing the request and its schedule time in a database, then using a cron job to check for work that is due.

With Schedules, an agent can create a schedule that records the request and when to run it, without a separate database and polling job. The example below defines an AI SDK tool that gives an agent this capability.

When the task is due, Vercel uses Queues to deliver the saved request to your app. Your app provides code to read that request, check the user’s current permissions, and start the agent. The agent fetches the top five Hacker News posts with a web tool, then returns a summary for your app to save for the user.

If you already build agents with fx’s JavaScript library, libfx or Pi’s agent library, you can add a similar scheduling tool. The eve agent framework uses Vercel Schedules to provide dynamic scheduling tools for production agents hosted on Vercel.

Run recurring application jobs

You can schedule recurring work with Vercel Schedules. Schedules can be created dynamically via the JS SDK, API, and CLI, or set up in your project’s configuration.

For example, to create a job that cleans up expired records every day, you could define a schedule that invokes a private function in your chosen time zone:

Vercel calls this cleanup code directly, without exposing it at a public URL. It checks that each call comes from the scheduling service, so you don’t have to add that check yourself.

If your app already uses the Nitro 3 server framework, its experimental integration lets you run the recurring jobs in your existing scheduledTasks configuration as private functions.

You can also try the agent task and cleanup locally with vercel dev, then test them on a Preview branch or in a custom environment before production. Use Run Schedule in your project’s Schedules tab to try either task without waiting, and see when past runs happened.

Get started

Vercel Schedules is now in Public Beta, and you can use it for the recurring tasks your application already runs. When a user or agent chooses when work should happen, your code can create and manage a schedule for that task.

To get started, check out the Vercel Schedules skill and read the documentation.

title: Vercel MCP now renders deployments as an interactive card
description:
Vercel MCP can now show your deployments as an interactive card inside ChatGPT and other chat clients that support MCP Apps.

The card shows live deployment status, build logs, and source and commit details, with a Visit button once the deployment URL is ready. You can send logs into the chat to debug with the model, or open the fullscreen view to read them beneath the card. For repositories linked to multiple projects, a project list lets you switch between them.

The card is Vercel MCP's first MCP App, built on the MCP Apps extension. Clients without app support receive the deployment state, preview URL, and commit as text instead. The open_deployments tool looks up deployments by project, repository, or commit, with environment filtering. ChatGPT connects to Vercel MCP through its Connectors setup.

title: Flags Explorer redesigned for easier override sharing
description:
Flags Explorer is a tool in the Vercel Toolbar where you can see which feature flags are active on your end, and share them with your team, either by setting them for the branch or through a URL.

The Explorer surface has been redesigned to co-locate overrides, branch recommendations, and any related actions.

Whenever a branch has overrides set, they will be recommended to teammates visiting the deployment through a dialog.

Flags Explorer is available on all plans. Read the documentation to get started.

description:
Vercel Sandboxes that mount Drives now start faster. Median creation time dropped from 1.7s to 0.7s, and p95 dropped from 2.2s to 1.6s.

The speedup applies automatically to every sandbox that uses Drives, with no SDK upgrade or configuration changes needed. Pricing stays the same.

title: Evaluate Vercel Flags from another project without sharing SDK keys.
description:
Project Connections let applications evaluate flags defined in another Vercel project within the same team, without managing SDK keys.

Previously, sharing flags between projects required copying a server SDK key into an environment variable and managing it manually. Connected projects authenticate using their deployment’s identity. For local development, vercel env pull retrieves your project’s OIDC token.

Manage access from the Connections page under your project's Flags section, or with vercel flags connections in the CLI. Connections grant read-only access across all environments. The consumer deployment determines the flag environment (production deployments evaluate production flags).

In the consumer application, create an adapter with the source project’s ID.

Access can be revoked without redeploying.

Project Connections are available on all plans and require @flags-sdk/vercel 1.6.0 or later, or @vercel/flags-core 1.11.0 or later when using the core library directly. Managing connections from the CLI requires Vercel CLI 63.0.0 or later.

Learn more in the Vercel Flags documentation

Read more

title: Blocking malicious npm packages before and during installation
description:
Vercel now checks for blocked npm packages before and during dependency installation in builds, helping prevent malicious install scripts from running.

The checks use a blocklist of specific package versions selected for blocking because of malware or security vulnerabilities, with new rules typically reaching new builds within minutes.

  • Before installation, Vercel checks supported lockfiles, including when dependencies are restored from the build cache.

  • During installation, Vercel blocks affected public npm downloads.

Existing checks of installed dependencies and function outputs continue before deployment.

These protections apply automatically to new builds on all plans, with no configuration required.

If a blocked dependency is detected, Vercel fails the deployment, identifies the package and version in the error, and attempts to invalidate the affected build cache. Update the dependency to a safe version and update the lockfile, then redeploy.

Read more

title: Introducing Geist Serif
description:
Geist started as a monospace typeface for developers, built for the editors and terminals where they spend their day doing their work. From there it grew into Geist Sans for product interfaces, and then into Geist Pixel, which was inspired by the grids of early computer screens.

Today, we're adding a new member to the family: Geist Serif.

Geist Serif is a high-contrast display serif built on the same foundations as Geist Sans, Geist Mono, and Geist Pixel. It has fine, saw-toothed serifs and sharp hairlines, and it was drawn to communicate messages powerfully both in the physical world and on the high-density screens on modern devices.

Same system, new voice

At Vercel, Geist Sans runs the product. For headlines, though, we wanted a second voice, one that belongs to the same system, instead of a stranger picked from a drop-down menu.

A lot of tech brands have moved away from clean sans-serifs to get some personality back, and many of them borrow from vintage computer ads. Geist Serif takes a different path: toward fashion, editorial design, and magazine headlines. It's our homage to the artists behind Rolling Stone and Harper's Bazaar.

From the beginning, each Geist family has read from a chapter of type history: the Swiss design movement, early terminal and DOS computing, and now editorial print.

Display first

Geist Serif began as a set of sketches by Evil Rabbit, which Andrés Briganti then expanded. The first letters already showed an expressive serif, in the spirit of typefaces like Victor Serif and Stanley.

When Mark Davis took over the drawings, we made the first release a display face for headlines, posters, and other large sizes, while work on the full family continued. Print has always struggled to hold fine hairlines and sharp serifs, but today's displays can handle a high level of detail. We wanted the new face to take full advantage of modern screens, so we thinned every downstroke by 50% and tightened the sidebearings to push the contrast as far as it would go.

Each serif has a wedge on one side and a curve on the other, so the proportions are classical and look beautiful in print, but the construction is new and optimized for digital devices.

From the first prototype to today

The first prototype of Geist Serif was shared on April 1, 2026. Here's the same word, Geist, in that prototype, compared with the display drawing shipping today.

Geist grew teeth

The goal was to honor our original intent and keep the serif closely tied to the sans, even when the letters sit on top of each other. Geist Serif’s stems match Geist Sans, and the two share widths and postures.

The saw-toothed serifs and high contrast give Geist an editorial voice. One phrase kept coming up as each character was drawn: “Geist grew teeth.”

Four families, one x-height

Geist Serif uses the same cap height and x-height as Geist Sans, so you can drop it into any Geist layout without moving a line. Mix Sans, Mono, Pixel, and Serif in the same sentence and every word looks the same size.

Four variants, one axis

Like Geist Pixel, Geist Serif has a variable axis that swaps the shape of every dot in the font, including those on i and j and in punctuation. The axis is called Element Shape (ELSH), and it gives you four variants: Regular with round dots (the default), Square, Triangle (a nod to the Vercel logo), and Heart.

Each variant also ships as its own static file. If you use the variable font, pick a variant with font-variation-settings:

Crafted by hand

In July the font had 227 glyphs. It now has 894 and covers 352 Latin-script languages, and we worked through more than 52,000 kerning pairs to get the spacing right. Some of the details are tiny. The eye of the g, for example, is tilted exactly 7°.

Specs at a glance

Geist Serif ships with:

  • 1 weight (Regular)

  • 4 variants (Regular, Square, Triangle, Heart)

  • 894 glyphs

  • 5 stylistic sets (ss01 to ss05)

  • 352 supported languages

Getting started

Geist Serif ships in the same package as the rest of the family:

Exports and CSS variables:

  • GeistSerif (variable, all shapes): --font-geist-serif

  • GeistSerifRegular: --font-geist-serif-regular

  • GeistSerifSquare: --font-geist-serif-square

  • GeistSerifTriangle: --font-geist-serif-triangle

  • GeistSerifHeart: --font-geist-serif-heart

Each one has its own entry point, so you only ship the font file you use. For example, in layout.tsx with GeistSerifRegular:

You can also download the font files, test every stylistic set, and inspect each glyph at vercel.com/font.

What’s next

Regular is the first style we’re releasing, and the rest of the family is already in progress. We’re testing future versions while building this one, so this release is just the start.

Weights from Thin to Black

The variable font will range from Thin (100) to Black (900). In this week’s proofs, the g in Black is the letter we can’t stop looking at.

Toward a text face

To explore a text version, we built a foundry tool that measures strokes, including where they meet, and thickens the display outlines. It edits the outlines directly, so we can set real words and see which strokes need more weight.

Italics, built rule by rule

We’re also developing an italic generated entirely in Python. We slanted existing italics back upright and compared them with their romans. With the angle removed, the remaining differences show up clearly, and we turned them into rules we can test and revise. This italic won’t be the final version, but breaking glyphs in code helps us find the limits faster.

More scripts and Google Fonts

Cyrillic support is planned to match Geist Sans and Geist Mono, and Geist Serif will come to Google Fonts after launch.

One family

With Geist Sans, Geist Mono, Geist Pixel, and now Geist Serif, the family runs from UI text and code to expressive display type, and all four feel at home together.

Download Geist Serif and start building.

Thank you to everyone who made Geist Serif possible.

None of this would have been possible without an incredible group of people behind the scenes.

Huge thanks to Andrés Briganti for starting this journey with me and drawing the first version that everything else grew from, and to Mark Davis for carrying it across the finish line with obsessive craft, from the expanded glyph set and variable axis to every last kerning pair. Thanks also to Patrick McDonald and Marijana Pavlinić for the poster designs, to Luis Gutierrez Rico for the motion and incredible magic, to Christopher Kindl for shipping the package and rebuilding the landing page down to the smallest details, and to Zahra Jabini for the coordination and technical support that brought it all together. This was a true team effort, and I’m grateful to have built it with all of you.

Strix, the open-source AI penetration testing tool, can now run on any of the 400+ models on Vercel AI Gateway.

Strix can reach models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Kimi, GLM, Deepseek, and others through a single API with no markup, removing the need to sign up for multiple providers. Usage and cost are tracked across all models in AI Gateway.
